subject.title: fix(net): cap default outbound HTTP connection pool limits

question: After repairing the Node construction-order bug, should OpenClaw impose global proxy defaults of 256 connections per origin and 1024 total sockets?
rationale: The mechanical defect is clear, but choosing shared throughput limits trades socket-exhaustion protection against queueing and timeout behavior across providers, plugins, and other callers; repository and dependency source cannot establish the intended product-wide values.

options.title: Fix and adopt the caps
options.body: Pass the limits at construction time and land only after redacted live concurrency proof shows bounded sockets without representative request failures.

options.title: Choose workload-informed limits
options.body: Repair the construction path but pause until maintainers select values based on expected provider, plugin, and proxy concurrency.

options.title: Keep dependency defaults
options.body: Drop the global policy and add limits only in narrower owners with observed socket-pressure failures.

recommendation.title: Fix and adopt the caps
recommendation.body: Pass the limits at construction time and land only after redacted live concurrency proof shows bounded sockets without representative request failures.
